profile.name: Mortefi
profile.introduction: Mortefi, a skilled expert in Applied Tacetite Study and a member of the Academy’s Department of Safety, possesses the unique ability to transform his accumulated frustration into fiery flames. From a burning wrath that consumes all, the red dragon shall descend.
profile.review:
Mortefi is a 4-star Fusion Pistol buffer character who specializes in buffing Heavy Attack damage. He also has access to some Coordinated Attacks and is well-known for being one of the best F2P characters since the game’s release.

Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts

Mortefi’s rotation goal is to get his Outro off as quickly as physically possible. To do this, he needs to charge up his Forte gauge, which allows him to cast a Forte Skill that generates a good amount of Concerto and deals some damage. He charges this Forte gauge up through his Intro, Basic Attacks, and Skill.

To charge it as quickly as possible, Mortefi should cast his Skill before any Basic Attacks. An Intro and a Skill already charge up a full Forte gauge, so he can cast a Forte Skill, while within 5s after casting his base Skill, Mortefi generates extra Forte through his Basic Attacks. A full Basic Attack string becomes enough for his next Forte Skill to be available, and at that point he has enough Concerto Energy to Outro if his Ultimate is also cast.

Speaking of his Ultimate, at S6 it gives an extra 20% ATK to the whole party on cast for 20s, it deals a bit of damage, and also it enables Mortefi to fire Coordinated Attacks at the enemy for 10 (S0) to 17 (S4) seconds. These Coordinated Attacks are triggered once by Basic Attack casts, twice by Heavy Attack casts, and also twice by Skill casts at S1. Overall, this allows Mortefi to fire off a good amount of Coordinated Attacks regardless of who he is paired with, but he does scale a bit better with Heavy Attack casters in this regard.

Finally, his Outro gives the next character 38% Heavy Attack DMG Amplification for 14s, expiring on swap. This is the main buff in his kit and makes or breaks his synergies. Mortefi’s passives give him a bit of extra personal damage, not much to explain there.

Meta Position & Conclusion

In the meta, Mortefi is super easy to understand. He’s completely one-dimensional and restricted to buffing Heavy Attackers, mostly through his Outro. He’s simple, but effective in his role. As a F2P buffing character, he sports a nice amount of generalist buffs: 38% Heavy DMG Amplification, and up to 52.5% ATK and 12% DMG Bonus with Moonlit Clouds, S6, and Static Mist all factored in.

Indeed, his best weapon being a permanent banner one gives him a good amount of usability in all endgame content alongside Heavy Attack damage dealers like Jingran, Yangyang: Xuanling, Augusta, or even his on-release partner Jiyan. Team DPS can vary pretty wildly based on how modern the damage dealer that he pairs with is. However, the more Heavy Attack damage dealers that release, the more Mortefi gains staying power, not as a best in slot option, but as a F2P replacement for all future Heavy Attackers to come.

In conclusion, Mortefi is a simple Heavy Attack buffer who can act as a potent buffer for all your Heavy Attack damage dealers. While never ideal in those teams, he can always replace a limited 5-star character to buff your DPS. If you’re in a pinch for teammates or have a modern enough DPS where you don’t need their dedicated Supports to clear endgame, Mortefi is a great choice, and is likely to remain that way in the future as long as Heavy Attack DPS characters release.
profile.pros:
• THE F2P Heavy Attack buffer. Buffs any Heavy Attack DPS you want him to and does it pretty well;

  • Has decent personal damage that can be invested into, but he works well out of the box with minimal resources invested into his build;

  • S4 and S6 are good, but he provides most of his value at S0 already. The permanent banner 5* Static Mist is his best in slot. TLDR: Super easy to get up and running.
profile.cons:
• Never best in slot for anybody. Expected out of a 4-star, but essentially if you own Rebecca, she’s just Mortefi but better (and you only have so many Heavy Attackers you could buff);

  • Rotation is somewhat long for a Hybrid (though quickswap is a possible avenue to compensate for this in some teams).

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Mortefi’s rotation goal is to quickly build up his Forte gauge, typically twice, in order to get his Outro off as quickly as possible.

Echo Timing

Swap Cancel Impermanence Heron right before Outro (written in the rotations themselves). On Empyrean Anthem, summon Hecate at any point in Mortefi’s rotation (after his Ultimate is recommended to benefit from the 20% ATK buff from S6).

Standard Rotation

  • Intro

  • Skill: Passionate Variation (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill: Fury Fugue (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate) 

  • Ultimate

  • Basic 1

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Skill: Fury Fugue (Cancel animation endlag via Echo)

  • Echo (Swap)

  • Outro

Additional Tips & Tricks

On Empyrean Anthem, Mortefi saves a bit of time by Swap Cancelling his Forte Skill instead of having to wait for the endlag to cancel it with his Echo cast.

Speaking of which, Mortefi’s rotation can be sped up in 2 ways: Either through Quickswap by building up Forte/Concerto ahead of time, or by interrupting his Forte Skills before they deal damage, as the Concerto is given on cast, not on hit.

However, his Forte Skills generate 10 Energy each. Considering that he casts 2 per rotation, not only are you forfeiting 20 Energy on Mortefi, you’re also forfeiting 10 Energy on your other 2 party members doing this. As a result, it’s generally not recommended unless you somehow have a lot of excess Energy Regen. However, you only need to interrupt 1 of 2 Forte Skills on Empyrean Anthem, so it could be a more realistic time-save on that set.

Mortefi’s rotation in Quickswap can utilize several tools, the most important of which being his Basic Attack strings. He starts on Basic 3 when swapped into in combat, so a quick Basic 3-4 is easy to fit in some other character’s swap window. In some niche cases, he can also cycle multiple Skill casts or even his Heavy Attack to interact with Jiyan’s Outro, for example. Feel free to experiment and see what works best based on your team.

skills.name: Impromptu Show
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Mortefi uses his dual guns and fire to perform up to 4 continuous attacks dealing Fusion DMG.

Heavy Attack

Mortefi enters the aiming state for a more powerful shot. The aimed shot fired after charging finishes deals Fusion DMG.

Mid-air Attack

Mortefi consumes Stamina to perform consecutive shots at the target in mid-air, dealing Fusion DMG.

Dodge Counter

Use Basic Attack after successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Fusion DMG.

skills.name: Passionate Variation
skills.description: Launch high-speed flame lightning forward, dealing Fusion DMG.

skills.name: Violent Finale
skills.description:
Deal Fusion DMG, and apply Burning Rhapsody to all characters in the team.

Burning Rhapsody

When the on-field character's Basic Attack hits the target, Mortefi launches a Coordinated Attack, firing 1 Marcato. When the on-field character's Heavy Attack hits the target, Mortefi launches a Coordinated Attack, firing 2 Marcato. Mortefi can launch one Coordinated Attack every 0.35s.

Marcato

Deals Fusion DMG.

skills.name: Fury Fugue
skills.description:
Resonance Skill: Fury Fugue

When Mortefi's "Annoyance" reaches 100, his Resonance Skill is replaced with Fury Fudge. When casting Fury Fudge, Mortefi consumes all "Annoyance" to unleash high-speed flame lightning, dealing Fusion DMG, considered as Resonance Skill damage.

Annoyance

Mortefi can hold up to 100 Annoyance. When Normal Attack Impromptu Show hits the target, “Annoyance” is restored. When Intro Skill Dissonance hits the target, “Annoyance” is restored. When Resonance Skill Passionate Variation hits the target, “Annoyance” is restored. Within 5 seconds after casting Passionate Variation, Basic Attack Impromptu that hits the target additionally restores “Annoyance”.

skills.name: Harmonic Control
skills.description: After casting Resonance Skill Passionate Variation, the damage of Resonance Skill Draconic Hellfire is increased by 25% for 8s.

skills.name: Rhythmic Vibrato
skills.description: During Resonance Liberation Burning Rhapsody, each hit of Resonance Liberation Marcato will increase the damage of the next Resonance Liberation Marcato by 1.5%, which can be triggered once every 0.35s, stacking up to 50 times. The effect will be reset after Resonance Liberation Burning Rhapsody ends.

profile.calculationsNotes: Mortefi does more damage depending on who he is supporting due to how his ultimate works. His ultimate can fire a maximum amount of 60 coordinated attacks at S0 in a literal perfect world when being abused by a Heavy Attack spammer, but this is not realistic, so we've used 35 coordinated attacks instead. This is how many you could expect to get when using Jiyan. Mortefi's S1 doesn't scale particularly well with Jiyan which is how we've represented but works much much better with characters like Danjin compared to what is shown here.

echoes.Comment: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.
echoes.Echo_2_Comment: Niche option used in tthe Jingran/Mortefi/Lupa team. Grants a Shield on cast which can activate Jingran's passive for a lot of Fusion DMG Bonus gained upon casting his Intro. Usually Swap Cancelled at the end of Mortefi's rotation.

echoes.Comment: Offers an unconditional 10% Energy Regen% and 80% Coordinated DMG boost. Also grants a passive supportive effect which triggers when the wearer of this set critically strikes with a Coordinated attack - this effect grants the on field Resonator an ATK% boost regardless if they're the wearer of the set or not. The set is better than Moonlit Clouds if and only if the equipped character's Echoes have endgame investment (with 9 or 10 CRIT substats total) and the character has a 5-star weapon equipped. If both conditions aren't met, Moonlit Clouds is a better choice.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Offers a 40% unconditional Coordinated Attack DMG% boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Coordinated Attack-focused resonators looking to use the 5P Empyrean Anthem Echo set bonus.

teams.Name: Zani Team
teams.Comments: Spectro Rover should be on Rejuvenating Glow.

synergies.Comment: Mortefi is by far the best F2P-accessible option for her as he provides a massive 38% Heavy Attack DMG Amplify on his Outro, which he accesses quickly and easily while retaining solid off-field personal damage via his Ultimate's Marcato Coordinated Attacks. As a pistol user, he additionally has access to an extra ATK% buff from the Static Mist weapon and he has an extra ATK% buff with his S6 as well, making him one of the best options by far.

As one of Galbrena's best partners, Mortefi provides 38% Heavy Attack DMG Amplify on his Outro which is one of Galbrena's 2 main damage types. Additionally, he can wield Moonlit Clouds and the Static Mist pistol for a ton of ATK% and DMG% buffing. On top of his fast rotation and solid personal damage, he makes for a fantastic Galbrena teammate in general, particularly with Lupa in a Mono Fusion setup.

Mortefi is Jiyan's tailor-made partner. Via his Echo Sets, his S6 and Static Mist, Mortefi can give lots of ATK% buffs, but most importantly he amplifies Jiyan's main damage type, Heavy ATK DMG, by 38% on Outro. Therefore, he buffs Jiyan's damage by large amounts and has amazung synergy with him.

Mortefi is a good secondary for Absolution Phoebe with a Rejuvenating Glow Spectro Rover, however his Heavy ATK DMG Amplify on Outro faces loads of diminishing returns so his buffing potential mostly lies in his S6 and potentially the Static Mist pistol so he provides lots of ATK% to Phoebe. Overall this pairing is one of the best for Absolution Phoebe, but it is contested.

Mortefi, in Zani teams, acts as a substitute for Phoebe's buffing effects, but unfortunately doesn't apply any Spectro Frazzle. To compensate for this, Mortefi with Zani must be used with Spectro Rover, but under these conditions the team can work just fine and is able to clear endgame content without any issues, so the trio is definitely usable for F2P accounts!

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
